Subject: Q-Eval Roadmap: latency/concurrency checkpoints + quant kernel results

Hi Alex —

Following our demo, attached is a proposed benchmarking & MAP draft (benchmark-plan-v1.pdf) that splits the work into three checkpoints:
- CP1 (perf baseline): FP16/BF16 runs at target sequence lengths and cold-start TTFT profile.
- CP2 (quant exploration): INT8 and INT4 experimental runs with kernel profile capture.
- CP3 (regression guardrails + canary): regression checks, KV-cache stress, and a canary deployment plan.

We want to validate these targets for Skyward production traffic:
- 99th-pct latency SLO at p95 inference: 220ms (single-request), 60ms steady-state per-token for streaming workloads
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) target: <= 300ms for cold path
- Concurrency slab targets: 16, 64, 192 simultaneous sessions for the three workload buckets

Can you confirm:
1) the test corpus (sample dataset link would be great)
2) acceptable regression thresholds for quality (LLM output tolerance vs baseline) — e.g. allowable BLEU/ROUGE drop or manual eval pass rate
3) procurement/PO timing that might affect our MAP close timeline

We’ll coordinate kernel profiling runs with Rishi and Marissa. Proposed sync: Mon 5/24 10am PT to review CP2 results.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Lead — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Attachment: benchmark-plan-v1.pdf (PDF, 1 page — MAP milestones + test matrix)

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear plan. Confirming a few items:
- Test corpus: we’ll share a de-identified snippet bucket (link: https://internal.skyward.ai/test-corpora/q-eval-sample). It mirrors our production prompts (multi-turn summaries + instruction-following).
- Quality guardrails: primary metric is manual human pass-rate (>= 92% vs baseline) + automated cosine similarity on embeddings (no more than 4% drop).
- Procurement: PO should land by 6/3; legal expects a final SOW before signature. That gives us a hard close target of 6/10 for CP3 rollout.

On quant expectations: we want to try INT8 for throughput gains; INT4 is acceptable only as an experimental branch — not for canary unless we pass automated regression checks and manual review.

I can join Mon 5/24 10am PT. Also looping in our infra lead if we need dedicated test hosts.

—Alex
Alex Chen

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Q-Eval Roadmap: latency/concurrency checkpoints + quant kernel results

Kim / Marissa —

Quick technical checklist ahead of 5/24 run:
- Kernel capture: enable kernel-level tracing on batch scheduler (trace id profile-q-2041). Capture per-layer runtimes, memory stalls.
- Quant profiles to run: FP16 (baseline), BF16 (if model supports), INT8 static/post-training aware, INT4 experimental (two-pass).
- Regression harness: 200 prompt eval set (hand-curated), automated token-level diff + RTT human spot-check (10 samples). Threshold: <= 3% automated metric delta OR human pass >= 92%.
- Stress: KV cache retention at 1k tokens, sampling concurrency at 192 for 60s window.
- Tooling: use redwood-bench v3.8 flags: --kv-cache --trace-kernels --concurrency-sweep=[16,64,192] --ttft-measure.

I’ll prepare a DRY-RUN script and the kernel profiler upload hook by EOD Mon. If we see INT4 regression on attention-kernel-3, we should auto-fail to INT8 and record the kernel stack for follow-up.

-Rishi
Principal Performance Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Alex Chen <alex@skyward.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Q-Eval Roadmap: latency/concurrency checkpoints + quant kernel results

On Mon, May 24, 2027 at 10:47 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks — jumping into CP2 now. Sharing preliminary runs as they complete.

Alex / Team —

We ran the CP2 matrix this morning across the requested concurrency slabs. Summary (attached qbench-skyward-5-24.csv):
- FP16 baseline: p50 latency 38ms, p95 210ms, TTFT cold 280ms at concurrency=16.
- INT8: throughput +42%, p95 latency improved to 145ms at moderate concurrency but TTFT increased ~10ms due to dequantization overhead.
- INT4 experimental: throughput +88% but one notable regression on a small fraction (~6%) of prompts flagged by the regression harness. Root cause: attention-kernel-3 under low-precision accumulates quant noise on long-context (>= 512 tokens).

Action items proposed:
1) Hold INT4 from canary. Promote INT8 with the following runtime flags: --quant-mode=int8 --fallback-kernel=attention-kernel-3:fp16 (will dynamically use FP16 for that kernel)
2) Add a focused eval subset of 50 long-context prompts for manual review (we’ll run today).
3) Schedule canary rollout for INT8 on 5/27 limited to 5% traffic; full rollout planned 6/02 if no regressions.

Attachment: qbench-skyward-5-24.csv (CSV, 12KB) — contains per-kernel timings and per-prompt regression flags.

-Marissa Cole
Sr. Applied ML Engineer — Redwood Inference
